units.spine: A traveller finds the market without asking the way, because the busiest road through the village ends among the stalls.
Armed order here is paid work rather than a favour asked of neighbours.
A household here can afford to argue about something other than money.
The village can get what it needs and move what it makes.
Hochhausen could hold what comes at it, though not for long.
The village is a match for ordinary trouble and is not armed for any other kind.
Every house here answers for its own fences, since nothing larger is organised against what lives beyond the fields.
More quarrels are opened here than are settled.
Nothing in the village is spare, and the want of it is the first thing a carter notices.
No practitioner is kept here, nor is anything in the village arranged around expecting one.
Bread here comes off fields the village owns, so a bad season would cost it more than a closed road.
The Commercial Circle and The Administrative Circle are at odds quietly enough that people passing through learn it late rather than on arrival.
Goods come in and goods go out at a pace that draws no remark.
A road runs through the village, so a good part of what the place lives on comes off the carts.
Villages of this kind settle at one size, and this one has settled there.
One tie here carries more weight than the rest, and the difference shows in what the village leaves undone.
People here are connected the way people in any settled place are, with nothing further to be made of it.
A careful eye finds one loose end in the village, and one office would be enough to tie it off.
